---
title: "Learning path"
subtitle: "How the course is organised, and what to study before what"
description: "The four levels of the course, the dependencies between modules and the full list of lessons with estimated study times."
---

The course grows in **four levels**. Each level uses the tools of the previous ones, and each lesson lists its own prerequisites at the top. The total self-study time is roughly **85 hours** (excluding the capstone), which matches a university module of up to 9 ECTS.

## The map

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Modules and their main dependencies. Solid arrows: required; dashed arrows: helpful."
flowchart LR
  subgraph L1["Level 1 · R foundations"]
    M1["1 · Getting started"] --> M2["2 · Working with data"]
    M1 --> M3["3 · Programming"]
    M2 --> M4["4 · Data in and out"]
  end
  subgraph L2["Level 2 · Describe & explore"]
    M5["5 · Descriptive statistics"] --> M6["6 · Visualisation"]
  end
  subgraph L3["Level 3 · Uncertainty & inference"]
    M7["7 · Probability & simulation"] --> M8["8 · Statistical inference"]
  end
  subgraph L4["Level 4 · Models & learning"]
    M9["9 · Regression models"] --> M10["10 · Supervised learning"]
    M11["11 · Dimensionality reduction"] --> M12["12 · Clustering"]
    M10 -.-> M13["13 · Deep learning (optional)"]
  end
  M4 --> M5
  M6 --> M7
  M8 --> M9
  M6 --> M11
  M3 -.-> M7
  M10 --> CAP(["Capstone project"])
  M12 --> CAP
```

## What each level gives you

| Level | You will be able to… | Key statistical ideas |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · R foundations** | write R code, organise a project, import, clean, reshape and summarise data | types of variables, units and observations, tidy data, missing-data mechanisms |
| **2 · Describe & explore** | describe a dataset with tables, numbers and graphics, and spot patterns | distributions, location and spread, robustness, association vs causation |
| **3 · Uncertainty & inference** | quantify uncertainty and test hypotheses, and explain results correctly | probability, sampling variability, standard error, CLT, bootstrap, CIs, p-values, power, effect sizes |
| **4 · Models & learning** | fit, check, compare and interpret statistical and machine-learning models | conditional means, GLMs, overfitting, cross-validation, regularisation, latent structure, clustering |
